title: Epic handoff
description: A cloud worker's claim about its epic: `.agents/handoff/<epic>.json`, one file per epic, on the epic's branch, changed as the epic moves (plan §3). It is a claim, not an authority. merge-check reads it at S and checks it against the bead database and the run files, and trusts the run file, not this copy of the lane result. `noetic-harness validate` checks it against this schema, and checks what the schema cannot state: the file is named for its `epic`; a `ready` handoff carries a `lane` whose verdict is `passed`, and no child still `open`; a `deferred` child has a `note` and a `reparented` one a `to`. Nothing here is checked against git or bd; that is merge-check's work.

epic.description: The epic's bead id. The file's name without `.json` must equal it.

profile.description: The worker profile the epic is assigned to, which is `HARNESS_AGENT` in the worker's environment and the `--agent` of its WF-021 run.

session.description: The cloud session the assignment names. merge-check compares the two, because two sessions of one profile can exist and the profile alone does not say which one did the work.

branch.description: `claude/<epic>-<slug>`, created from origin/develop by the epic's first commit.

base_develop.description: Informational: origin/develop when the branch was created or last merged it. Nothing is checked against it; merge-check computes the merge-base itself.

status.description: `working` from the first commit. `blocked` while it waits on `questions`, and the session ends `EPIC <id> BLOCKED <reason>`. `ready` only in the branch's last commit, S, written after the WF-021 run finished, and the session ends `EPIC <id> READY <S> <pr-url>`.

children.description: Every child of the epic, and what became of it. `open` is a working state and never a ready one: `noetic-harness validate` refuses a `ready` handoff with an `open` child, and merge-check refuses the landing.

outcome.description: `done`: finished in this branch, and the landing closes it. `deferred`: not done here and left open for later, with the reason in `note` (required, checked by `noetic-harness validate`). `reparented`: belongs under another epic, named in `to` (required, checked the same way). `open`: not yet decided, which is allowed only before `ready`.

commits.description: Full shas of the commits that did it. A short sha can become ambiguous in a repository that keeps growing.

to.description: For `reparented`: the bead the child moves under.

discovered.description: Work found while doing this epic that is not part of it. Workers never write beads, so this is where a new bead comes from: the coordinator files each entry when it lands the epic.

questions.description: What the worker needs the coordinator or the person to answer. A `blocked` handoff is blocked on the ones marked `blocking`. The answer comes back as a message into the session, not as an edit to this file.

shared_change_requests.description: Changes this epic needs in paths outside its scope and grants: another profile's, or one the coordinator holds. The worker does not make them; it names the paths and says why, and the coordinator relays each one.

runs.description: The ids of this epic's harness runs, its WF-021 run among them. merge-check reads each one from S, and the run files, not this list, are what it believes.

lane.description: A copy of the finished WF-021 run's lane result, written after `--finish`. Required when `status` is `ready`, which `noetic-harness validate` checks because the schema cannot. merge-check reads the run file, not this copy.

seconds.description: The run's `gates.seconds`: the lane's wall clock.

head.description: The run's `gates.head`: the commit the lane ran at. S may differ from it only by handoff and run files.

gates.description: The run's `gates.results`, id and outcome only.
